tagline.text: Negros's largest forest, home to Mandalagan and Silay volcanoes

location.label: Location
location.text: Northern highlands of Negros Occidental (Silay, Talisay, Murcia and Salvador Benedicto areas)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Day waterfall trek or overnight mountain trek

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–5,000 (including trek permit and guide, estimated per person)

children.text: A protected area of about 80,000 hectares in the northern highlands of Negros Occidental, with the Mandalagan volcanic complex, Mount Silay and forest waterfalls. It is the watershed that supplies water to the Bacolod area and home to birds and deer found only on Negros.
Northern Negros Natural Park is a protected area in the northwestern highlands of Negros Island. It lies about
40km

east-northeast of Bacolod and covers roughly 80,454 hectares. It spans many cities and towns, including Silay, Talisay, Murcia, Salvador Benedicto, Calatrava, Sagay and San Carlos, so the scenery and the starting point change completely depending on which side you enter from.

The forest was first declared a forest reserve on April 28, 1935, and was reduced to its current size in 1946. In 2005 it became a natural park under the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act and is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR). It is the largest watershed in Negros Occidental, supplying water to 17 cities and municipalities, including the Bacolod metropolitan area. For travelers, it helps to remember that before it is a sight, this is the forest that produces drinking and irrigation water for local residents.
The terrain centers on Mount Mandalagan (about
) and Mount Silay (about

). Mandalagan is a stratovolcano with several craters and calderas, and the caldera called Tinagong Dagat, which fills with water in the rainy season, is a popular camping destination for hikers. Old-growth forest remains above
in elevation, and four rivers, the Malogo, Imbang, Himoga-an and Bago, cross the lower slopes.

However, only about 16,687 hectares of intact forest remain today, and about 48 percent of the park is human-dominated land such as farmland. So this is not a national park with a single gate and ticket booth. Instead, you climb into the forest from villages and farms behind them. Depending on your goal, the options range from an easy day waterfall walk to a full mountain climb that requires a permit. What makes the place special is its wildlife. It is known to shelter endangered animals such as the Visayan spotted deer, the Visayan warty pig and the Negros shrew, along with endemic birds such as the Visayan hornbill, the Negros bleeding-heart and the Visayan flowerpecker. Plants include dipterocrats, palms, orchids, tree ferns and almaciga. Wildlife is shy, however, so it is not easy to see on a short visit.

This is the most representative waterfall walk, reached on foot with a guide from Patag in Silay City. The water and rocks have a reddish tint, which gave the falls their name, meaning "red water." You can see farm trails turn into forest in one go, which makes it the easiest choice for a day trip.

blocks.title: Mount Mandalagan and the Tinagong Dagat caldera

children.text: The summit area of the volcano, at about

above sea level, has several craters large and small. Tinagong Dagat, which fills with water in the rainy season, is a destination for hikers who camp and watch the stars. This is a serious climb that requires a permit and a guide.
This stratovolcano, about
above sea level, can be reached by the Silay–Lantawan Road. It forms the northern axis of the park, and on clear days the ridge looks down over the northern Negros plains and the sea.

The park is reported to have about 140 bird species, roughly 40 percent of which are found only on Negros. Birdwatchers searching for species such as the Visayan hornbill and the Negros bleeding-heart visit the forest edge early in the morning.

blocks.title: Forest trail from farmland to old-growth forest

children.text: The entrance area is fields and village, but about
10 minutes
after you start walking, the forest thickens. You can see the habitat change from forest edge to old growth with your own eyes, which is good for travelers interested in ecology.

This route climbs from Salvador Benedicto, known as the "summer capital" of the Negros Occidental highlands. Under the official permit rules, this entry point is also listed as available every week. Hiking apps list the route from here up Mandalagan as a difficult course.

blocks.title: Permit-based climbs rotating among entry points

children.text: The official trails rotate weekly among Patag (Silay), Campuestuhan (Talisay) and Canlandog (Murcia), while Kumaliskis (Salvador Benedicto) is open every week. So when planning your schedule, first check which entry point is open that week.

items.title: Day course
items.subtitle: Guided trek from Patag to the waterfall

children.text: Take a bus or jeepney bound for Silay from the Bacolod North Terminal. The ride to Silay is said to take about
45 minutes–1 hour
Look for the jeepney to Patag at the Silay market. It often leaves only when full, so it is best to go early.
Arrive in Patag, sign the logbook at a resort or park information point at the entrance, and find a guide.
Walk the forest trail with your guide. You begin on farmland, enter forest after about
10 minutes
, and then reach a section where you cross a river, so be prepared to get wet.
Rest and have lunch at the waterfall. One traveler's account says getting there takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
Come back down the same way and leave the village before the last jeepney.
Jeepneys to Patag are reported to run only during daytime hours. Be sure to confirm the return schedule locally.
Email the booking form to DENR-PENRO Negros Occidental.
Submit all documents and get your orientation certificate of completion.

Meet your guide and porter at the entry point and start climbing. Hiking apps note that on the Salvador Benedicto side there are possible camping spots at the grassland (DSB Grassland) or the nursery.
Explore the Tinagong Dagat caldera area, then descend. The schedule can stretch depending on weather and fitness.
Climbing requires a permit, and the rules change often. Check the latest announcement before you leave.
There are direct flights from Manila to Bacolod-Silay Airport (BCD), with a flight time of about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check before booking.
The airport is in Silay, so it is closest to Patag, the northern entrance of the park.
If you are coming from Cebu or Dumaguete, you can also combine a ferry and overland travel, so check locally.
Take a bus or jeepney bound for Silay from the Bacolod North Terminal. Many sources say it takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
Jeepneys to Patag leave from the Silay market area. Older sources put the fare at about ₱45.
From Silay to Patag is about
32km
, and travelers report the jeepney ride takes about
1 hour–2 hours 30 minutes
Travelers report that hiring a vehicle for the day costs around 10 times a jeepney ride. The driver may not know the way, so choose a driver who knows Patag.
From Bacolod, go up to the highland town of Salvador Benedicto by car or local transport and use the Kumaliskis entrance. Check locally for exact routes and fares.
Hiking app sources describe January to July as the suitable period for climbing Mandalagan. In the dry season the trail is less slippery and the caldera is easier to reach.
A waterfall walk can be hard to do right after heavy rain because the river crossing becomes difficult. The rivers can rise in the rainy season, so follow your guide's judgment.

Lodging falls in two directions. You can stay in Silay or central Bacolod and make a day trip, or stay at a highland resort in Salvador Benedicto. Patag has small resorts and campsites, and some people stay there the night before a climb. In peak season or on weekends, contact them in advance.

Eat in town before you go up, and bring plenty of packed food and water. There are no shops in the forest. After coming down, Silay's historic streets and Bacolod's restaurant districts are good places to enjoy local food.
A climb requires a DENR permit and an orientation. The policy is that you cannot climb without completing the orientation.
Permit requirements include a health certificate, a notarized waiver and a booking form. Start booking at least 2 weeks ahead.
On the day waterfall course there are sections where you get wet, so bring sandals or shoes that drain well. Some travelers recommended walking barefoot on the rocky river section.
A waterproof bag, a change of clothes, a rain jacket and plenty of drinking water are basics. You must carry out all your trash, and for a climb you will sign a zero-waste commitment form.
Guide fees go to local residents. Keeping to the set rates and using a local guide is good for navigation, safety and the local economy.
Jeepneys sometimes run only in daytime, so be sure to confirm the return time. It is safer to arrange a hired vehicle in case your descent runs late.
Wildlife is not easy to see, so keep your expectations low and enjoy the birdsong early in the morning.
Rules change often. Check the latest announcements from DENR-PENRO Negros Occidental for fees and permit procedures.
Formal climbs such as Mandalagan cannot be done without a permit. Booking, paperwork and orientation are all required, so prepare well in advance.
Mandalagan is a volcano with craters and fumaroles. Do not stray from your guide's directions on the summit area.
Rivers can rise suddenly when it rains. If it looks dangerous, do not force a crossing and turn back.
Leeches, insects and slippery rocks are common in the forest. Bring long clothing and non-slip shoes.
Many sections have weak mobile signal. Share your route with your guide and carry emergency contacts.
Climbing rules and open entry points have changed on a weekly basis. Check with DENR right before your visit.
This is the gateway to the park's northern entrance. It is about
45 minutes–1 hour
from Bacolod by car and has a cluster of historic houses and churches.
A cathedral in central Silay, nice to visit before or after a trek.
The main city of Negros Occidental, with the airport, terminals, lodging and restaurants, making it the base for climbs.
The ruins of a mansion in Talisay, in the same city as Campuestuhan, the park's southern entrance, so the two can be combined.
